A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SuperEvent and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and supplementary appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite added experiments, renumbering, and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original pose-estimation experiments, TUM-VIE SLAM results, runtime measurements, and ablations of training data, event representations, and network architectures.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds VECtor SLAM evaluation, adverse-condition comparisons, relative pose errors, and a homography-estimation analysis.

M1.justification: Temporal pseudo-label generation, MCTS construction, the MaxViT/FPN architecture, detector and descriptor heads, losses, NMS, and OKVIS2 integration remain unchanged. Compiled float16 runtime testing changes execution settings without introducing a new method component.

E1.justification: v2 adds large-scale VECtor SLAM evaluation and an actual HVGA ATIS homography experiment, whereas v1 only discusses the latter dataset. It also extends TUM-VIE evaluation to mocap-shake, mocap-shake2, and floor2-dark, testing fast-motion and low-light operation. Training coverage and the ECD/EDS pose-estimation tasks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds plain frame-based OKVIS2 using BRISK as a quantitative comparator. Appendix C also explicitly contrasts SuperPoint plus SuperGlue with SuperEvent under adverse imaging conditions. The original pose-estimation and TUM-VIE comparator sets remain unchanged; VECtor comparisons reuse DEIO and ESVO.

E3.justification: Runtime evaluation changes from plain PyTorch measurements on ECD/EDS to compiled float16 inference across four cropped input resolutions. v2 adds consecutive-sample RPE, SLAM comparisons at 20 and 40 Hz, and a homography protocol using 400 keypoints, 50 ms separation, and five RANSAC thresholds. The original training recipe and pose-estimation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix C tests matching under HDR and fast motion, SLAM under fast motion and low light, and sensitivity to processing rate. Figure 9 adds a RANSAC-threshold analysis relating reprojection error to inlier ratio. The original training-data, representation, architecture, and loop-closure ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs and selection of the median-error trajectory for small-scale TUM-VIE experiments. v2 introduces no new seed information, uncertainty intervals, error bars, significance tests, or repeated-run procedure.

E6.justification: Original pose-estimation, TUM-VIE ATE, and ablation table values are retained, while v2 adds VECtor, RPE, robustness, and homography results. For example, Table 10 reports mocap-shake ATE of 43.71 cm for SuperEvent versus 50.83 cm for frame-based OKVIS2 at 20 Hz. The previous 2.9 ms inference and 0.2 ms NMS figures are replaced by resolution-dependent 1.3–23.2 ms inference and 0.4 ms NMS under changed execution settings, not a same-setting speed comparison.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), the pose-sampling construction, and the argument about homography reprojection error remain substantively unchanged. The added RANSAC experiment provides empirical support rather than a new definition, derivation, or proof.

C1.justification: The introduction broadens the third contribution from outperforming event-based SLAM approaches on TUM-VIE to doing so on TUM-VIE and VECtor. The central claims about temporal supervision, MCTS, robust descriptors, and integration into frame-based SLAM retain their meaning.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly explains higher-rate performance through increased temporal overlap and reduced motion-dependence effects. v2 also qualifies RPE results when ground truth is discontinuous and explains their omission for loop-floor sequences. The existing limitation concerning descriptor matching under strong motion changes remains.

D1.justification: v2 documents compilation, float16 precision, runtime input cropping, online calibration for VECtor, and settings for the added experiments. It changes the advertised project/code address from the Smart Robotics Lab host to the ETH MRL host. Existing optimizer, training duration, hardware, and model hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds the VECtor benchmark citation and removes the U-Net citation previously included among methods using homographic adaptation. The broader related-work organization and positioning against existing event detectors, trackers, and odometry systems remain stable.

P1.justification: v2 makes grammatical and terminology corrections, updates affiliations, and consolidates runtime reporting into the implementation discussion. It inserts an event-versus-frame appendix and shifts the former Appendices C/D to D/E. Most existing paragraphs and the main narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds displays for runtime scaling, VECtor results, adverse-condition comparisons, RPE, and RANSAC sensitivity, including a new matching-example figure and six VECtor trajectory panels. Existing method diagrams and result tables remain; the former trajectory Figures 8–9 become Figures 10–11, with layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation of the paper’s practical motivation. Appendix C adds direct, same-rate comparisons against frame-based OKVIS2 under fast motion and low light, addressing a gap in v1, while VECtor evaluation extends downstream validation beyond TUM-VIE. More specific runtime reporting and explicit ground-truth caveats improve interpretability. Cross-rate RPE values use different temporal intervals, limiting that particular comparison, but the broader validation provides a clear substantial quality gain.
